To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CdTe nanocrystals are grown on the surfaces of MWNTs via in situ chemical coordination of the nanocrystals to the nanotubes, and the resulting nanocrystal/nanotube heterostructures demonstrate a controlled synthetic route toward the generation of nanoscaled interconnects.
we have demonstrated a novel method of synthesizing CdTe quantum dots directly onto the surfaces of oxidated multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWNTs) using a coordination approach.

the chemical coordination of metallic precursors of CdTe quantum dots onto the surfaces of oxidize MWNTs and then proceeding with in situ growth of quantum dots on the nanotubes is a novel approach toward the synthesis of complex, nanoscale heterojunctions.

the development of a novel, rational approach toward the synthesis of complex nanostructures.
the development of novel nanosystem architectures and the fundamental understanding of the interplay of chemistry and physics at the nano- and molecular scale.
the design and synthesis of novel nanosystems that will enable the development of new nanoscale technologies.

this study demonstrates a controlled synthetic approach to the generation of nanoscaled, molecularly engineered supramolecular, nanohybrid materials.
the nanocrystal-nanotube heterostructures are a unique system with potential applications in the fields of nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, and nanobiotechnology.
the in situ synthesis of CdTe nanocrystals on the surfaces of MWNTs provides an effective method of generating nanotube-nanostructure heterostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated a novel synthetic approach toward the fabrication of complex heterostructures of MWNTs and semiconductor quantum dots.
this study demonstrates the ability of a rational, chemical approach to the synthesis of a novel, hierarchical nanomaterial that can potentially be used in a variety of applications.
the in situ growth of quantum dots on MWNTs is an effective approach to fabricate a novel nanoscale heterojunction.

the in situ growth of nanoscale heterojunctions is a viable route to the synthesis and assembly of complex nanosystems.
we can use the chemical affinity of the nanotube and nanocrystal surfaces to create nanoscale assemblies with controlled dimensions and properties.
the nanoscale interfacial interactions between the nanoscale components of the system are strong enough to enable the formation of the heterostructures.
